name: Moong Dal

ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more as needed
ground red chile powder, preferably Kashmiri

weigh_parts.name: fresh lime juice, from 1 large lime plus more as needed

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince the ginger. Peel and mince the garlic. Chop the yellow onion. Cut the ripe plum tomatoes into 1-inch pieces. Juice the lime.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (5 cm) piece ginger
5 medium cloves garlic
1 medium yellow onion
2 medium ripe plum tomatoes
½ lime

instructions.primary_message: Place mung beans in a large bowl and cover by 5 cm cool water. Using your hands, vigorously swish mung beans until water turns cloudy, taking care to remove any stones or grit, about 30 seconds. Using a fine-mesh strainer, drain mung beans, discarding cloudy water. Repeat until water runs clear, 3 or 4 more times. Return mung beans to a bowl and add enough cool water to cover by 8 cm; soak at room temperature at least 2 hours and up to 12.

Using a fine-mesh strainer, drain mung beans. In a medium pot or Dutch oven, combine mung beans, 6 cups water, ground turmeric, and salt. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium and simmer until beans have cracked open slightly, about 30 minutes. (They should not be mushy.)

For the Masala: In a medium saucepan heat oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add asafoetida, cumin seeds, and mustard seeds. Cook, allowing the seeds to sizzle and pop, about 10 seconds, then add ginger and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, 1 minute. Add green chile and onion and cook, stirring frequently, until translucent and beginning to soften, 3 to 4 minutes. Add coriander and chile powder, and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook until softened and broken down, 3 to 4 minutes.

Transfer masala to cooked mung beans and stir to combine. Bring to a simmer and season to taste with salt and lime juice as needed. Remove from heat, then stir in cilantro and 1 tablespoon ghee. Serve immediately with white rice, roti, or as an accompaniment to any Indian meal.

description: Spiced with turmeric and flavored with a fragrant onion and tomato masala, moong dal is an aromatic dish that’s a staple in many South Asian households, including mine.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 2 hr 45 min.

Optional or for serving: Cooked white rice, such as basmati or jasmine (optional); Roti (optional)

Notes: Whole dried mung beans are available online and at many South Asian grocery stores.

Make-ahead and storage: Moong dal can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Moong dal can be frozen in an airtight container for up to 3 months; to thaw, place in fridge overnight. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.
author: Rachel Gurjar
